detailed_description: The Readability Checker analyzes pasted plain text directly in the browser and shows practical readability signals for quick editing passes. The visible results include Flesch-Kincaid grade, Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog, SMOG, estimated reading time, word count, sentence count, and character count. It also displays simple suggestions when sentences are long, words are complex, or the reading level looks high. Use it for blog drafts, help-center articles, documentation summaries, landing-page copy, and classroom handouts when you want a fast readability check before publishing. The calculator uses simple sentence, word, and syllable heuristics, so treat the numbers as editing guidance rather than a certified language assessment.
usage_steps: Paste the paragraph, article excerpt, help text, or documentation section into the text box.
Review the Flesch-Kincaid grade, Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog, SMOG, reading time, and basic text counts.
Read the interpretation panel to see whether the draft looks easy, moderate, or difficult for a general audience.
Use the suggestions to shorten long sentences, replace complex words, or adjust the text for the intended reader.
Paste the revised version again and compare the new scores before moving the copy into your CMS, docs, or design mockup.
usage_examples: A product marketer checks whether a landing-page section has drifted above the intended reading level before handing it to design.
A technical writer compares two versions of an API guide intro and keeps the one with clearer sentence length and reading ease.
A support lead reviews a help-center answer for shorter sentences before publishing it to customers.

faqs.question: What readability scores does this page show?
faqs.answer: The current interface shows Flesch-Kincaid grade, Flesch Reading Ease, Gunning Fog, SMOG, reading time, word count, sentence count, and character count.

faqs.question: Does it rewrite or grammar-check my text?
faqs.answer: No. It calculates readability metrics and displays editing suggestions, but it does not rewrite sentences, check grammar, or replace a human editor.

faqs.question: Are the scores exact for every language?
faqs.answer: The formulas and syllable heuristics are most useful for English-style readability checks. For other languages, use the result as a rough signal rather than a final quality score.

faqs.question: Is the text uploaded to a server?
faqs.answer: The calculation runs in the browser from the text you paste into the page. Avoid pasting confidential material into any online tool unless your workflow allows it.
